筆.meaning: A lighthouse keeper ties a fat <part>brush</part> to a long <part>bamboo</part> pole, dips it in the sea and paints huge letters across the clouds: HELLO, SHIPS. Sailors can read it for miles. That's some <kanji>writing</kanji>.
筆.on: A <sound>hitch</sound>hiker on the cliff reads it and sticks out his thumb at a passing boat.
筆.kun: Afterwards the keeper naps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton out on the <sound>de</sound>ck, brush in hand.

探.meaning: A lost sailor is sure his treasure chest is somewhere in the woods. He drags his ship's <part>anchor</part> along the ground, throws a fishing <part>net</part> over every <part>tree</part>, and shakes out squirrels, kites and one grumpy owl. No chest yet. The <kanji>search</kanji> goes on.
探.on: Next he digs a long <sound>tun</sound>nel under the roots.
探.kun: In the dark he finds a <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin, still <sound>goo</sound>d to eat, and keeps groping about.

吸.meaning: A tired lifeguard sits by the pool with a <part>catch net</part> for leaves, but it's far too slow. So he opens his <part>mouth</part> wide and slurps: leaves, a rubber duck, two goggles and half the water. He can really <kanji>suck</kanji>.
吸.on: Out pops a pool <sound>cue</sound> that someone dropped in last summer.
吸.kun: Then he slurps the <sound>soo</sound>t off the chimney next door.

衛.meaning: At the busiest <part>crossroads</part> in the land, a tall <part>pagoda</part> stands guard. Its monks keep buckets of custard on every tier and tip them over any army that marches through. Not one has got past. It's the kingdom's best <kanji>defense</kanji>.
衛.on: Squirrels on the roof drop one hard <sound>a</sound>corn each on the soldiers' helmets.

即.meaning: A <part>robot</part> clerk has a rubber <part>stamp</part> for a hand. Slap, slap: every form is approved before you've finished your sentence. Passport? Done. Fishing licence? Done. Results in an <kanji>instant</kanji>.
即.on: It even stamps the <sound>sock</sound> you drop on its desk.
即.kun: It stamps the <sound>soo</sound>t on your hand, your <sound>na</sound>an bread and your baby's '<sound>Wah</sound>!': that is to say, everything.

季.meaning: A <part>child</part> plants one stalk of <part>grain</part> and sits beside it with a stopwatch. Green, then gold, then cut, then snow, then green again: she times each one and writes it in her notebook. She's timing the <kanji>seasons</kanji>.
季.on: Every year she locks the notebook with the same brass <sound>key</sound>.

査.meaning: A detective squirrel climbs a <part>tree</part> with a magnifying glass. 'Footprints on this branch,' she notes, 'and <part>moreover</part>, crumbs. And moreover, a sock.' The list goes on and on. She loves to <kanji>investigate</kanji>.
査.on: The crumbs lead to a half-eaten <sound>sa</sound>rdine in a hollow.
